Title: How to choose the right way to install gh on Linux: official packages, community builds, and one strongly discouraged path
Description: The source cleanly divides installation methods into three classes—Recommended (official Debian/RPM/Homebrew/precompiled), Community (distribution-maintained or third‑party packages), and Discouraged (Snap). A practical explainer can help readers decide which class to use based on support expectations and platform availability, using only the facts and warnings given in the document.
Audience: Linux desktop users, developers, and sysadmins deciding how to install GitHub CLI (gh) on their systems.
Rationale: The document itself organizes installation options into Recommended, Community (Unofficial), and Discouraged sections and repeats who maintains each package. That structure supports a focused piece that translates those categories into practical decision criteria (which installers are maintained by GitHub CLI maintainers, which are community-maintained, and which to avoid). This helps readers make an evidence-based choice without adding external claims.
Evidence:
• The header sections: ‘Recommended (Official)’, ‘Community (Unofficial)’, and ‘Discouraged’.  
• Explicit statements that Debian/RPM/Homebrew packages are “supported by the GitHub CLI maintainers” and updated via the project’s deployment workflow (links to cli.github.com and deployment workflow).  
• The Community section begins with an IMPORTANT note: “The GitHub CLI team does not maintain the following packages… We are unable to provide support…” and then lists many distro-specific packages.  
• The Discouraged section contains a WARNING: the team “actively discourages use of the following methods” and specifically states “never installing gh as a snap” with a link to issues describing problems.
